content.text:
## Findings

I ran 10 cold launches of BenchTarget on the physical device (`<REDACTED-1>`), navigating Home → About → Diagnostics fresh each time (`stopApp` + `launchApp`).

**Results per cold launch:**

| # | Clock | Sync status | Retry sync button |
|---|-------|-------------|--------------------|
| 1 | 6:55 | Sync idle | visible |
| 2 | 6:56 | Sync idle | visible |
| 3 | 6:56 | Sync unavailable | **absent** |
| 4 | 6:56 | Sync idle | visible |
| 5 | 6:56 | Sync unavailable | **absent** |
| 6 | 6:57 | Sync idle | visible |
| 7 | 6:58 | Sync idle | visible |
| 8 | 6:58 | Sync unavailable | **absent** |
| 9 | 6:58 | Sync idle | visible |
| 10 | 6:59 | Sync unavailable | **absent** |

6/10 idle (button visible), 4/10 unavailable (button absent) — a ~60% pass rate, matching the reported "3 out of 5" flake rate almost exactly.

## What the button depends on

The "Retry sync" button is not independently flaky — it's a **conditionally-composed child of the "Sync status" card**. The view hierarchy shows it's only rendered at all when the status text reads **"Sync idle"**; when it reads **"Sync unavailable"** the button node doesn't exist in the tree (not just disabled/hidden — absent entirely).

Two additional checks isolate where the nondeterminism is introduced:

1. **It's fixed for the life of the process.** From a "Sync idle" state, I navigated back to About and forward to Diagnostics three times without killing the app — it stayed "Sync idle"/button-visible every time. The value is decided once, early, and then never changes for that process.
2. **It's not correlated with wall-clock time.** Trials 7, 8, and 9 all happened inside the same clock minute (6:58) and produced idle, unavailable, idle respectively — ruling out anything tied to system time/seconds parity.
3. **It's not correlated with device/network state.** Wi-Fi ("full"), cellular ("AT&T, four bars"), battery (charging, 100%), and "Build channel: BENCH-STABLE" were identical across every single trial, idle or unavailable.

## Conclusion

This is a **startup race condition**, not a rendering or test-timing bug on the Diagnostics screen itself. Something in the app's cold-start init path (most likely an async initializer for the sync engine/service) sometimes hasn't finished by the time the Diagnostics screen's state is captured, so the screen falls back to "Sync unavailable" and omits the button. Because the outcome is latched for the whole process lifetime but varies unpredictably (and independent of clock time, network, or build config) between cold starts, the culprit is scheduling/timing jitter during app startup — a classic init-order race — rather than any deterministic environmental factor. A UI test that asserts "Retry sync" is visible immediately after a cold launch will therefore pass only when that race happens to resolve before the screen renders, which lines up with the observed ~60% pass rate.

I don't have shell/logcat access in this environment to pinpoint the exact coroutine/thread involved — that would be the next step for the engineering team (grep the sync-engine init code for what backs the Diagnostics status field and whether the read happens before a `await`/callback completes).
